ai.description: This snake reaches 20–30 cm. It is dark brown or purplish with yellow lateral spots and a blunt, shield-like tail tip. A small, pointed head distinguishes it from the cylindrical body.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Uropeltis ceylanica* is distinguished by its blunt, shield-like tail ending in a distinct, bicarinate (two-ridged) terminal scale, which lacks the spines found in other genera.
ai.habitat: Cuvier's Shieldtail inhabits the moist evergreen forests and high-altitude grasslands of the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations between 600 and 2,000 meters.
ai.behavior: Cuvier's Shieldtail is primarily nocturnal and fossorial, spending most of its time burrowing through loose soil to forage for earthworms.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Uropeltis ceylanica* is viviparous, typically producing a small litter of 3–9 young. Breeding occurs primarily during the monsoon season, from June to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Uropeltis ceylanica* is endemic to the southern Western Ghats of India, primarily occurring in the states of Kerala and Tamil Nadu at elevations of 600–2,000 meters.
